QF.id: VII Market Participants in Securities Markets_20

question.text: An 'insider' under SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 is defined as:

answer.text: A connected person OR any person in possession of or having access to unpublished price sensitive information
Only a director or officer of a listed company
Only a person who has traded based on UPSI
An employee of SEBI who monitors market activity

explanation.text: The Logic: An insider is defined as (i) a connected person, OR (ii) any person in possession of or having access to UPSI, regardless of how they obtained it. The definition deliberately casts a wide net. The Trap: You do not need to be a company employee or director to be an insider; any person with access to UPSI is covered, regardless of designation or how the information was obtained. Note: The initial onus to show that the person was in possession of or had access to UPSI at the time of trading is on the person levelling the charge. Once that is shown, the trader may demonstrate non-possession, no trade, lack of access, or an exonerating circumstance, as stated in the pages checked (56-57).
